title: Amplification of the bass in the 1930s and 40s
summary: Some basses used amplifiers like the Ampeg, but Stewart mostly relied on the house system.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, in those days did they, how was -- how was -- was the bass amplified in performance in those years?

At times, yes. At times a couple of the basses had amplifiers, and most of the time, of course, myself, I just used the house system where we were playing. Most of the -- a few of the basses had those Ampegey.
Yeah, I think the Ampegey came about in the late '30s, yeah. *
Oh, yes? Because that was around the time that Charlie Christian, I think --
I can't remember what it's called. He had some kind of an amplifier, though.
It was a Gibson he had.
Uh-huh. And so some guys were using the Ampegey, though.
Ampegey, yes. Then further on they had, the Ampegey company, I think, made those little baby basses, you know, the frame, basses on a small frame?
*Everett Hull developed the AMPEG PICKUP AND amplifier around 1950 or '51. (there were earlier pickups.)
